LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.IsAchievableRate: For a channel W with finite output alphabet, a rate R is achievable if R ≥ 0 and there is one sequence of deterministic block codes with message counts Mₙ ≥ 1 whose uniform-message average error tends to zero and whose rates eventually reach or exceed R − δ for every δ > 0.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.isAchievableRate_: For any channel with nonempty input alphabet and finite output alphabet, rate zero is achievable by a code with one message at every blocklength.
For a channel with finite alphabets and nonempty input alphabet, every rate R with 0 ≤ R < C(W) is achievable by deterministic block codes with vanishing average error.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.le_channelCapacit: For a channel with finite alphabets and nonempty input alphabet, every achievable rate R satisfies R ≤ C(W).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.isLUB_isAchievabl: For a channel with finite alphabets and nonempty input alphabet, C(W) is the least upper bound of all achievable rates, including when C(W) = 0.
